proofs.proof_tex:
For (a\in\mathcal A), let \(\mu_a\) be the marginal law of \((Y_t(a),D_t(a))\).  By \texttt{ass:iid-arrivals}, the current potential outcome--delay vector is independent of \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\) and has its common law.  By \texttt{ass:sequential-randomization}, assignment is conditionally independent of that current vector given \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\).  Consequently, if \(Z_t=(Y_t(W_t),D_t(W_t))\), then for every measurable set \(B\),
\[
 P\{W_t=a,Z_t\in B\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}\}
 =\pi_t(a)\mu_a(B).                                                    \tag{1}
\]
After \((W_t,Z_t)\) is drawn, its revelation time and revealed record are the measurable functions
\[
 V_t=t+D_t(W_t),\qquad
 (t,W_t,V_t,D_t(W_t),Y_t(W_t)).                                         \tag{2}
\]
Thus, for every possible delayed history \(h_{t-1}\), the transition kernel first draws \(a\) with probabilities \(\pi_t(a;h_{t-1})\), then draws \(z\) from \(\mu_a\), and finally schedules the record according to (2).

On an auxiliary probability space, take two independent sequences
\[
 \{Z_{a,j}:j\geq1\},\qquad Z_{a,j}\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}\mu_a,
 \qquad a\in\{0,1\}.                                                     \tag{3}
\]
At time \(t\), after the policy chooses \(W_t=a\), consume \(Z_{a,N_a(t)}\).  Conditional on the observed delayed history and on \(W_t=a\), this unused entry is independent of the history and has law \(\mu_a\).  Hence the tape construction has exactly the kernel (1).  Induction over \(t=1,\ldots,T\) proves equality of the joint laws of all assignments, logged propensities, scheduled revelation times, and records revealed by every calendar time through \(H_T\).  In particular, it proves equality of the laws of \(O_{T,\Delta}\).

No independence between the two potential arms within one arrival was used: only the marginal selected by \(W_t\) occurs in (1).  This explains why the independent tapes reproduce the observed law even if the two potential pairs in the original arrival vector are dependent.  By (3), every deterministic prefix of each tape is an iid arm sample and the two prefixes are mutually independent.  This is unconditional; no event concerning the times at which tape entries are consumed has been conditioned upon.

For the finite-support stress test, take \(T=2\).  Let the second assignment probability take one value if the first outcome has already been revealed and is positive, another if it has been revealed and is nonpositive, and a third if it remains pending.  For every assignment pair \((a_1,a_2)\) and every pair of tape atoms \((z_1,z_2)\), both constructions give the cylinder probability
\[
 \pi_1(a_1)\mu_{a_1}(z_1)
 \pi_2\{a_2;h_1(a_1,z_1)\}\mu_{a_2}(z_2).                              \tag{4}
\]
The history \(h_1\) uses the outcome in \(z_1\) only when the delay component makes it observable.  Equality (4) holds atom by atom without factorizing the outcome and delay in \(z_1\), verifying the asserted reduction under reward-dependent switching.

Write \(I_t(a)=\mathbf 1\{W_t=a\}\).  Predictability and sequential randomization permit an inverse-transform realization with independent \(U_t\sim\operatorname{Unif}(0,1)\) such that
\[
 I_t(1)=\mathbf 1\{U_t\leq\pi_t(1)\},
 \qquad I_t(0)=\mathbf 1\{U_t>\pi_t(1)\}.                               \tag{1}
\]
For arm one set \(Z_t(1)=\mathbf 1\{U_t\leq ct^{-\alpha}\}\).  Under either model class, the applicable lower allocation envelope gives \(Z_t(1)\leq I_t(1)\) almost surely.  For arm zero set \(Z_t(0)=\mathbf 1\{U_t>1-\varepsilon\}\).  On \(\mathfrak M_T^{\mathrm{low}}\), \texttt{ass:control-floor} gives \(Z_t(0)\leq I_t(0)\).  On \(\mathfrak M_T\), \texttt{ass:rare-arm-envelope} and \(C\leq1-\varepsilon\) give
\[
 \pi_t(0)=1-\pi_t(1)\geq1-Ct^{-\alpha}\geq1-C\geq\varepsilon,          \tag{2}
\]
so the same domination holds.  For either arm, the variables \(Z_t(a)\) are independent Bernoulli variables with means \(e_a(t)\), and
\[
 N_a(s)\geq S_a(s):=\sum_{t\leq s}Z_t(a)\quad\hbox{almost surely}.       \tag{3}
\]

Fix \(a,s\), write \(Q=Q_a(s)\), and let \(0<x<Q\).  Independence and exponential Markov inequality give, for every \(\lambda>0\),
\[
 P\{S_a(s)\leq Q-x\}
 \leq \exp\{\lambda(Q-x)+Q(e^{-\lambda}-1)\}.                           \tag{4}
\]
Set \(u=x/Q\) and \(\lambda=-\log(1-u)\).  Since
\[
 (1-u)\log(1-u)+u\geq\frac{u^2}{2},\qquad 0\leq u<1,                    \tag{5}
\]
where (5) follows by differentiating and using \(-\log(1-u)\geq u\), (4) yields
\[
 P\{S_a(s)\leq Q-x\}\leq\exp\{-x^2/(2Q)\}.                            \tag{6}
\]
At \(s=n_T\) and \(s=k_T\), one has \(Q_a(s)/\log T\to\infty\).  Therefore, for all sufficiently large \(T\), the maximum with (2) in the definition of \(K_a(s)\) is inactive.  Taking \(x=\sqrt{8Q_a(s)\log T}\), (3)--(6) then give
\[
 P\{N_a(s)<K_a(s)\}\leq T^{-4}.                                       \tag{7}
\]
There are two arms and two deadlines, so the union bound proves
\[
 P(E_T^c)\leq4T^{-4}.                                                     \tag{8}
\]

Finally, because \(0\leq\alpha<1\), integral comparison gives
\[
 \sum_{t\leq s}t^{-\alpha}
 =\frac{s^{1-\alpha}}{1-\alpha}\{1+o(1)\}.                             \tag{9}
\]
Also \(n_T=T-\lfloor T^\rho\rfloor\sim T\), \(k_T=\lfloor T^\rho\rfloor\sim T^\rho\), and \(\sqrt{Q_a(s)\log T}=o\{Q_a(s)\}\) at both deadlines.  Substitution in the quota formula gives
\[
 K_1(n_T)\asymp T^{1-\alpha},\qquad K_0(n_T)\asymp T,
 \qquad J_1\asymp T^{\rho(1-\alpha)},\qquad J_0\asymp T^\rho.          \tag{10}
\]
All bounds depend only on the fixed envelope constants, so (8)--(10) hold uniformly over both declared classes.

Work with the unconditional tape representation supplied by \texttt{lem:arm-tape-equivalence}.  Since \(m_T=k_T=\lfloor T^\rho\rfloor=o(T)\), for all sufficiently large \(T\),
\[
 0\leq g_{T,\Delta}<h_{T,\Delta},
 \qquad h_{T,\Delta}=T+\Delta_T-k_T.                                    \tag{1}
\]
The tape entries in each arm are identically distributed.  Therefore the fixed-prefix definitions imply
\[
 \mathbb E_P M_{a,\Delta}
 =\mathbb E_P[Y(a)\mathbf 1\{D(a)\leq g_{T,\Delta}\}],
\]
\[
 \mathbb E_P U_{a,\Delta}
 =\mathbb E_P[Y(a)\mathbf 1\{g_{T,\Delta}<D(a)\leq h_{T,\Delta}\}].    \tag{2}
\]
The two indicator sets in (2) are disjoint and their union is \(\{D(a)\leq h_{T,\Delta}\}\).  Hence
\[
 \mathbb E_P(M_{a,\Delta}+U_{a,\Delta})
 =\mathbb E_P[Y(a)\mathbf 1\{D(a)\leq h_{T,\Delta}\}],                \tag{3}
\]
which is the asserted mean identity.

By \texttt{ass:bounded-outcomes} and \texttt{ass:polynomial-delay-envelope},
\[
 \left|\mathbb E_P[Y(a)\mathbf 1\{D(a)>h_{T,\Delta}\}]\right|
 \leq P\{D(a)>h_{T,\Delta}\}
 \leq\min\{1,L(1+h_{T,\Delta})^{-\beta}\}.                            \tag{4}
\]
Applying the triangle inequality to the two arms gives \(|b_{T,\Delta}|\leq B_{T,\Delta}\).  Moreover,
\[
 \frac{1+h_{T,\Delta}}{1+T+\Delta_T}
 =1-\frac{k_T}{1+T+\Delta_T}=1+o(1)                                    \tag{5}
\]
uniformly over deterministic \(\Delta_T\geq0\).  Because \(h_{T,\Delta}\to\infty\), the minimum in \(B_{T,\Delta}\) is eventually inactive.  Thus
\[
 B_{T,\Delta}=2L(1+T+\Delta_T)^{-\beta}\{1+o(1)\}.                     \tag{6}
\]

For
\[
 R=Y(a)\mathbf 1\{g_{T,\Delta}<D(a)\leq h_{T,\Delta}\},
\]
the same two assumptions give
\[
 \mathbb E_P R^2\leq P\{D(a)>g_{T,\Delta}\}
 \leq v_{T,\Delta}.                                                      \tag{7}
\]
Consequently, \(\operatorname{Var}_P(U_{a,\Delta})\leq v_{T,\Delta}/J_a\).  The two arm tapes are independent, so
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_P(U_{1,\Delta}-U_{0,\Delta})
 \leq v_{T,\Delta}(J_1^{-1}+J_0^{-1}).                                  \tag{8}
\]
Since \(g_{T,\Delta}\geq m_T\asymp T^\rho\), (7) implies \(v_{T,\Delta}=O(T^{-\rho\beta})\), uniformly over nonnegative follow-up sequences.  The quota orders in \texttt{lem:quota-success} now yield
\[
 v_{T,\Delta}(J_1^{-1}+J_0^{-1})
 =O\!\left(T^{-\rho(\beta+1-\alpha)}\right).                           \tag{9}
\]
The definition of \(\rho\) states
\[
 \rho>\frac{1-\alpha}{1-\alpha+\beta},
\]
which is equivalent to \(\rho(\beta+1-\alpha)>1-\alpha\).  Thus (9) is \(o(T^{-(1-\alpha)})\), proving all assertions uniformly over the stated classes.

Write \(K_a=K_a(n_T)\), \(J_a=K_a(k_T)\), and define the unconditional virtual tape statistics
\[
 \sigma_{a,T}^2=\operatorname{Var}_P(X_{a,1}^{\Delta}),
 \qquad
 Z_T=(M_{1,\Delta}-\mathbb E_PM_{1,\Delta})
      -(M_{0,\Delta}-\mathbb E_PM_{0,\Delta}),
\]
\[
 C_T=(U_{1,\Delta}-\mathbb E_PU_{1,\Delta})
      -(U_{0,\Delta}-\mathbb E_PU_{0,\Delta}).                           \tag{1}
\]
By the arm-tape lemma, these use deterministic prefixes of two independent iid tapes.  By the old-cohort lemma, on \(E_T\),
\[
 \widehat\tau_{T,\Delta}-\tau+b_{T,\Delta}=Z_T+C_T.                    \tag{2}
\]

First, the delay envelope excludes infinite delays.  Continuity from above and \(\beta>0\) give, for each arm,
\[
 P\{D(a)=\infty\}=\lim_{u\to\infty}P\{D(a)>u\}
 \leq\lim_{u\to\infty}L(1+u)^{-\beta}=0.                              \tag{3}
\]
We next verify measurability.  On \(E_T\), the first \(K_a\) assignments to arm \(a\) occur no later than \(n_T\), so their ages at \(H_T\) are at least
\[
 H_T-n_T=m_T+\Delta_T=g_{T,\Delta}.                                     \tag{4}
\]
The first \(J_a\) assignments occur no later than \(k_T\), so their ages are at least
\[
 H_T-k_T=h_{T,\Delta}.                                                    \tag{5}
\]
If such a response is revealed, \(O_{T,\Delta}\) records its outcome, delay, and revelation time.  If it is absent at \(H_T\), (4) or (5) shows that its delay exceeds the relevant truncation age, so its truncated contribution is known to be zero.  Hence every \(X_{a,j}^{\Delta}\), \(R_{a,j}^{\Delta}\), sample variance, gate, and endpoint is \(O_{T,\Delta}\)-measurable on \(E_T\).  On \(E_T^c\), the prescribed values depend only on observed assignment counts.  Thus the complete interval is measurable.

We next establish the concentration branch.  If \(X\in[-1,1]\), the chord bound for the exponential, followed by centering, gives
\[
 \mathbb E_P e^{\lambda(X-\mathbb E_PX)}\leq e^{\lambda^2/2}.           \tag{6}
\]
Multiplying (6) over the independent tape entries and optimizing exponential Markov inequality gives, with \(S_T=K_1^{-1}+K_0^{-1}\),
\[
 P\{|Z_T|>\sqrt{2S_Tx}\}\leq2e^{-x}.                                  \tag{7}
\]
For an old-tail variable \(R\), boundedness and the delay envelope imply
\[
 |R-\mathbb E_PR|\leq2,qquad
 \mathbb E_P(R-\mathbb E_PR)^2\leq\mathbb E_PR^2\leq v_{T,\Delta}.     \tag{8}
\]
For every integer \(j\geq2\),
\[
 \mathbb E_P|R-\mathbb E_PR|^j
 \leq2^{j-2}\mathbb E_P(R-\mathbb E_PR)^2.                              \tag{9}
\]
Expanding the exponential series, using \(j!\geq2\,3^{j-2}\), and optimizing the resulting Chernoff bound yields
\[
 P\left\{|U_{a,\Delta}-\mathbb E_PU_{a,\Delta}|>
 \sqrt{\frac{2v_{T,\Delta}x}{J_a}}+\frac{4x}{3J_a}\right\}
 \leq2e^{-x}.                                                            \tag{10}
\]
The displayed linear term is at least the optimized Bernstein linear term, so (10) follows directly from (8)--(9).  With \(x=x_\eta=\log(6/\eta)\), the union of the exceptional events in (7) and the two instances of (10) has probability at most \(\eta\).  On its complement, (2), \(|b_{T,\Delta}|\leq B_{T,\Delta}\), and the triangle inequality imply coverage by \(I_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm{conc}}\) whenever \(E_T\) occurs.  Intersection with \([-2,2]\) cannot remove \(\tau\in[-2,2]\), and on \(E_T^c\) the reported interval is \([-2,2]\).  This argument is unconditional.

It remains to establish the Gaussian branch and the observable splice.  Put
\[
 V_T=\sigma_{1,T}^2+mathbf 1\{\alpha=0\}\sigma_{0,T}^2.                \tag{11}
\]
Consider any triangular sequence for which \(V_T\geq1/\log T\).  If \(\alpha>0\),
\[
 s_{T,\Delta}^2\geq\frac{1}{K_1\log T};                                 \tag{12}
\]
if \(\alpha=0\), the deterministic quota orders imply
\[
 s_{T,\Delta}^2\geq\frac{c_0}{T\log T}                                 \tag{13}
\]
for a fixed \(c_0>0\).  Express \(Z_T/s_{T,\Delta}=\sum_j\xi_{Tj}\) as the sum of its independent centered tape summands.  Their variances sum to one.  By boundedness, (12)--(13), and \(K_1\asymp T^{1-\alpha}\),
\[
 \delta_T^*:=\max_j|\xi_{Tj}|
 =O\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log T}{K_1}}\right)=o(1)\quad(\alpha>0),
\]
\[
 \delta_T^*=O\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log T}{T}}\right)=o(1)
 \quad(\alpha=0),                                                        \tag{14}
\]
uniformly over this variance regime.  For fixed \(u\in\mathbb R\), Taylor expansion with remainder bounded by \(|u|^3\delta_T^*\mathbb E_P\xi_{Tj}^2/6\) gives
\[
 \mathbb E_Pe^{iu\xi_{Tj}}
 =1-\frac{u^2}{2}\mathbb E_P\xi_{Tj}^2
 +O\!\left(|u|^3\delta_T^*\mathbb E_P\xi_{Tj}^2\right).              \tag{15}
\]
Also
\[
 \sum_j(\mathbb E_P\xi_{Tj}^2)^2
 \leq(\delta_T^*)^2\sum_j\mathbb E_P\xi_{Tj}^2=(\delta_T^*)^2.        \tag{16}
\]
Taking logarithms in (15), summing, and using (14)--(16) proves uniformly that
\[
 \mathbb E_P\exp\{iuZ_T/s_{T,\Delta}\}=e^{-u^2/2+o(1)}.                \tag{17}
\]
The unit second moment gives tightness.  Every subsequential limit is identified by (17) as standard normal; a contradiction-subsequence argument, using continuity of \(\Phi\), therefore gives
\[
 \sup_{V_T\geq1/\log T}\sup_{x\in\mathbb R}
 \left|P\{Z_T/s_{T,\Delta}\leq x\}-\Phi(x)\right|\longrightarrow0.   \tag{18}
\]
Thus the normal limit has been derived from bounded summands and deterministic quota growth; no convergence of \(t^\alpha\pi_t(1)\) has been assumed.

The correction can overlap the main prefix, so independence of \(C_T\) and \(Z_T\) is not asserted.  Instead, the old-cohort variance bound gives
\[
 \mathbb E_PC_T^2=O\!\left(T^{-\rho(\beta+1-\alpha)}\right).            \tag{19}
\]
Combining (12)--(13) with (19),
\[
 \frac{\mathbb E_PC_T^2}{s_{T,\Delta}^2}
 \leq C_1(\log T)T^{1-\alpha-\rho(\beta+1-\alpha)}\longrightarrow0,    \tag{20}
\]
because \(\rho(\beta+1-\alpha)>1-\alpha\).

For a sample of size \(K\geq2\), the usual sample variance satisfies
\[
 \widehat\sigma^2=\frac{K}{K-1}(\overline{X^2}-\bar X^2).
\]
Since \(|X|\leq1\), Chebyshev's inequality applied to \(\overline{X^2}\) and \(\bar X\) gives, uniformly in the tape law,
\[
 \widehat\sigma_{X,a,\Delta}^2-\sigma_{a,T}^2=O_P(K_a^{-1/2}).          \tag{21}
\]
If \(\alpha>0\), division of the two contributions to \(\widehat s^2-s^2\) by (12) bounds their relative orders by
\[
 O_P(\log T/\sqrt{K_1})=o_P(1),
 \qquad O_P(K_1\log T/K_0^{3/2})=o_P(1).                                \tag{22}
\]
If \(\alpha=0\), both quotas are comparable to \(T\), and (13) gives the same conclusion.  Hence
\[
 \widehat s_{T,\Delta}/s_{T,\Delta}\longrightarrow1                    \tag{23}
\]
uniformly on \(V_T\geq1/\log T\).  Equations (2), (18), (20), and (23), together with \(P(E_T^c)\leq4T^{-4}\), give the uniform studentized approximation on this regime.  Replacing the quotient by zero on \(E_T^c\) changes its distribution function by at most \(P(E_T^c)\).

The regular class eventually lies in this high-variance regime.  Indeed, with \(X=Y\mathbf 1\{D\leq g_{T,\Delta}\}\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 |\operatorname{Var}_P(X)-\operatorname{Var}_P(Y)|
 &\leq|\mathbb E_P(X^2-Y^2)|
   +| (\mathbb E_PX)^2-(\mathbb E_PY)^2|\\
 &\leq3P\{D>g_{T,\Delta}\}\leq3v_{T,\Delta}=o(1).
 \end{aligned}                                                           \tag{24}
\]
The last equality is uniform because \(g_{T,\Delta}\geq m_T\to\infty\).  The regular-variance assumption therefore gives \(V_T\geq\kappa/2\) eventually, with the two arm bounds in (24) added when \(\alpha=0\).  This proves both studentization assertions on \(\mathfrak M_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm{reg}}(\kappa)\).

For coverage, define for \(B\geq0,s>0\)
\[
 f_B(s)=s c_\eta(B/s).                                                     \tag{25}
\]
If \(Z\sim N(0,1)\), the defining equation for \(c_\eta\), together with monotonicity in the absolute shift, implies for every \(|b|\leq B\),
\[
 P\{|sZ-b|\leq f_B(s)\}
 =\Phi\{c_\eta(B/s)+b/s\}+\Phi\{c_\eta(B/s)-b/s\}-1
 \geq1-\eta.                                                             \tag{26}
\]
Let \(u=B/s\) and \(x=c_\eta(u)-u\).  The defining equation implies
\[
 z_{1-\eta}\leq x\leq z_{1-\eta/2},
 \qquad B+z_{1-\eta}s\leq f_B(s)\leq B+z_{1-\eta/2}s.                  \tag{27}
\]
Implicit differentiation gives
\[
 c_\eta'(u)=
 \frac{\phi(c_\eta(u)-u)-\phi(c_\eta(u)+u)}
 {\phi(c_\eta(u)-u)+\phi(c_\eta(u)+u)}\in[0,1].                        \tag{28}
\]
Moreover,
\[
 f_B'(s)=x+
 \frac{2u\phi(x+2u)}{\phi(x)+\phi(x+2u)}.                               \tag{29}
\]
This derivative is uniformly bounded because \(x\geq z_{1-\eta}>0\) and
\[
 \frac{\phi(x+2u)}{\phi(x)}=e^{-2ux-2u^2}.                              \tag{30}
\]
Thus (23) implies
\[
 f_{B_{T,\Delta}}(\widehat s_{T,\Delta})
 -f_{B_{T,\Delta}}(s_{T,\Delta})=o_P(s_{T,\Delta})                      \tag{31}
\]
uniformly on the high-variance regime.  Combining (18), (20), (23), (26), and (31) gives
\[
 \inf_{V_T\geq1/\log T}P\{\tau\in I_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm G}\}
 \geq1-\eta-o(1).                                                        \tag{32}
\]
Formally, shrink the deterministic Gaussian interval in (26) by \(\epsilon s_{T,\Delta}\), use the Kolmogorov error in (18), (20), and (31), and then let \(\epsilon\downarrow0\); the Gaussian probability loss is at most \(2\epsilon/\sqrt{2\pi}\).  The nonnegative term \(d_{T,\Delta}\) only enlarges the interval.

The quota orders and the two strict inequalities defining \(\rho\) give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 d_{T,\Delta}
 &=O\!\left(T^{-\rho(\beta+1-\alpha)/2}\sqrt{\log T}
          +T^{-\rho(1-\alpha)}\log T\right)\\
 &\quad+O\!\left(T^{-\rho(\beta+1)/2}\sqrt{\log T}
          +T^{-\rho}\log T\right)
 =o(T^{-(1-\alpha)/2}).
 \end{aligned}                                                           \tag{33}
\]
It remains to validate the data-dependent splice.  If \(V_T\leq1/\log T\), (21) and Chebyshev's inequality imply
\[
 \sup_{V_T\leq1/\log T}P(G_{T,\Delta})
 \leq C_2(\log T)^2/K_1\longrightarrow0.                                \tag{34}
\]
Indeed, gate success requires the relevant sample-variance sum to exceed its population counterpart by at least \(1/\log T\); for \(\alpha=0\), apply the same argument to the sum of the two errors.

If \(V_T>1/\log T\), then on \(G_{T,\Delta}^c\), the gate inequality and \(\widehat\sigma^2\leq2\) give
\[
 \widehat s_{T,\Delta}^2
 \leq\frac{2}{K_1\log T}+\frac{2}{K_0}
 =o(T^{-(1-\alpha)})\quad(\alpha>0),                                    \tag{35}
\]
while for \(\alpha=0\),
\[
 \widehat s_{T,\Delta}^2
 \leq\frac{2}{\log T}(K_1^{-1}+K_0^{-1})=O((T\log T)^{-1}).             \tag{36}
\]
Since \(a_T=\sqrt{2S_Tx_\eta}\asymp T^{-(1-\alpha)/2}\), equations (33), (35), and (36) imply for all sufficiently large \(T\), on gate failure,
\[
 f_{B_{T,\Delta}}(\widehat s_{T,\Delta})+d_{T,\Delta}
 \leq B_{T,\Delta}+z_{1-\eta/2}\widehat s_{T,\Delta}+d_{T,\Delta}
 \leq B_{T,\Delta}+a_T.                                                  \tag{37}
\]
The concentration radius is at least \(B_{T,\Delta}+a_T\), so on gate failure the concentration interval contains the Gaussian interval.  Therefore (32) proves honesty of the selected interval in the high-variance regime.  In the low-variance regime, the concentration argument following (10), minus the vanishing probability (34), proves honesty.  Finally, \([-2,2]\) on \(E_T^c\) covers \(\tau\) identically.  This proves uniform honesty over both model classes, unconditionally and without propensity convergence.

Let \(Z\sim N(0,1)\).  For \(c'>0\) and \(u\geq0\),
\[
 P\{|Z-u|\leq c'\}=\Phi(c'-u)+\Phi(c'+u)-1.                             \tag{1}
\]
The derivative of the right side with respect to \(u\) is \(\phi(c'+u)-\phi(c'-u)\leq0\).  For fixed \(u\), it is continuous and strictly increasing in \(c'\), from zero to one.  This proves existence and uniqueness of \(c_\eta(u)\), and its defining equation gives exact coverage \(1-\eta\) at a shift of magnitude \(u\).

Now let \(\Delta_T=0\) and \(\beta=q=(1-\alpha)/2\).  On \(\mathfrak M_{T,0}^{\mathrm{reg}}(\kappa)\), the regular variance condition, the truncation comparison
\[
 |\operatorname{Var}_P(Y(a)\mathbf 1\{D(a)\leq g_{T,0}\})
   -\operatorname{Var}_P(Y(a))|
 \leq3P\{D(a)>g_{T,0}\}=o(1),                                          \tag{2}
\]
and the deterministic quota orders give constants \(0<c_0<C_0<\infty\) such that
\[
 c_0T^{-2q}\leq s_{T,0}^2\leq C_0T^{-2q}.                              \tag{3}
\]
The old-cohort lemma gives \(B_{T,0}=O(T^{-q})\), so \(B_{T,0}/s_{T,0}\) is uniformly bounded.  The uniform studentized approximation, \(\widehat s_{T,0}/s_{T,0}\to1\), the bounded derivative of \(s\mapsto s c_\eta(B/s)\) proved in \texttt{thm:uniform-gated-inference}, and \(|b_{T,0}|\leq B_{T,0}\) imply from (1) that
\[
 \inf_{(P,\Pi,T)\in\mathfrak M_{T,0}^{\mathrm{reg}}(\kappa)}
 P\{\tau\in I_{T,0}^{\mathrm G}\}\geq1-\eta-o(1).                   \tag{4}
\]
The additional radius \(d_{T,0}=o(T^{-q})=o(s_{T,0})\) is nonnegative and hence cannot decrease coverage.

We now construct an attaining family.  Use the deterministic policy
\[
 \pi_t(1)=ct^{-\alpha},\qquad \pi_t(0)=1-ct^{-\alpha},                  \tag{5}
\]
and put \(\delta_T=L(1+T)^{-q}\), which is less than \(1/2\) for all sufficiently large \(T\).  Index the laws by \(\zeta\in\{-1,1\}\).  In arm one, with probability \(\delta_T\), set \((D,Y)=(T+1,\zeta)\); conditional on \(D=0\), let \(Y\in\{-1,1\}\) have mean \(-\zeta\delta_T/(1-\delta_T)\).  In arm zero, with probability \(\delta_T\), set \((D,Y)=(T+1,-\zeta)\); conditional on \(D=0\), let \(Y\in\{-1,1\}\) have mean \(\zeta\delta_T/(1-\delta_T)\).  Take the arrival vectors iid over \(t\); the two arms may be taken independent within an arrival.

All outcomes are bounded and all delays are finite.  For integer \(0\leq u\leq T\),
\[
 P\{D(a)>u\}=\delta_T\leq L(1+u)^{-q},                                  \tag{6}
\]
and for \(u\geq T+1\) this probability is zero.  Thus the polynomial envelope holds, although outcome and delay are dependent.  In each arm the visible and hidden means cancel and \(Y^2=1\), so
\[
 \mathbb E_PY(1)=\mathbb E_PY(0)=0,
 \qquad \operatorname{Var}_P(Y(1))=\operatorname{Var}_P(Y(0))=1.        \tag{7}
\]
Thus the family satisfies every design and sampling condition, and lies in the regular class whenever the stated bounded-support floor is feasible.

Since \(g_{T,0}<h_{T,0}<T+1\), every old-cohort correction variable is zero.  Taking \(\zeta=1\),
\[
 \tau=0,\qquad b_{T,0}=2\delta_T,
 \qquad \operatorname{Var}_P(X_{a,1}^{0})=1-\delta_T-\delta_T^2.        \tag{8}
\]
Therefore
\[
 s_{T,0}^2=(1-\delta_T-\delta_T^2)(K_1^{-1}+K_0^{-1}),                  \tag{9}
\]
and, because \(h_{T,0}=T-k_T\),
\[
 \frac{b_{T,0}}{B_{T,0}}
 =\left(\frac{1+h_{T,0}}{1+T}\right)^q\longrightarrow1.                \tag{10}
\]
Integral comparison in the quota formula gives
\[
 \frac{K_1}{T^{1-\alpha}}\longrightarrow\frac{c}{1-\alpha},
 \qquad \frac{K_0}{T}\longrightarrow\varepsilon.                      \tag{11}
\]
Equations (9)--(11) yield
\[
 \frac{B_{T,0}}{s_{T,0}}\longrightarrow u=
 \begin{cases}
  2L\sqrt{c/(1-\alpha)},&\alpha>0,\\
  2L(c^{-1}+\varepsilon^{-1})^{-1/2},&\alpha=0,
 \end{cases}                                                            \tag{12}
\]
which is finite and strictly positive.

The bounded independent triangular-array calculation in the proof of \texttt{thm:uniform-gated-inference}, together with quota success and sample-variance consistency, gives
\[
 \frac{\widehat\tau_{T,0}-\tau+b_{T,0}}{s_{T,0}}\Rightarrow N(0,1),
 \qquad \frac{\widehat s_{T,0}}{s_{T,0}}\longrightarrow1.              \tag{13}
\]
Combining (10)--(13),
\[
 \frac{\widehat\tau_{T,0}-\tau}{s_{T,0}}\Rightarrow N(-u,1),
 \qquad \frac{B_{T,0}}{s_{T,0}}\longrightarrow u.                      \tag{14}
\]
Since \(\tau=0\) is in the interior of \([-2,2]\), while \(\widehat\tau_{T,0}\to0\) and all radii vanish, truncation at the parameter-space boundary is asymptotically irrelevant.  For every fixed \(c'>0\), (1), (13), and (14) imply
\[
 P\{\tau\in[\widehat\tau_{T,0}\pm c'\widehat s_{T,0}]\}
 \longrightarrow\Phi(c'-u)+\Phi(c'+u)-1.                               \tag{15}
\]
By (1), \(c'=c_\eta(u)\) gives equality \(1-\eta\), and every smaller symmetric critical value has strictly smaller endpoint-shift coverage.  This proves attainment at the phase boundary.

Because \(|Y(a)|\leq1\), \(\operatorname{Var}_P\{Y(a)\}\leq1\).  Thus nonemptiness of \(\mathfrak M_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm{reg}}(\kappa)\) requires \(\kappa\leq1\) if \(\alpha>0\), and \(\kappa\leq2\) if \(\alpha=0\).  Conversely, under the respective restriction, take prompt symmetric Rademacher outcomes in both arms, zero delays, and \(\pi_t(1)=ct^{-\alpha}\).  Then \(\pi_t(0)\geq1-c\geq\varepsilon\), so this law belongs to the regular class and proves sufficiency of the feasibility restriction.

On the regular class, the variance comparison
\[
 |\operatorname{Var}_P(Y(a)\mathbf 1\{D(a)\leq g_{T,\Delta}\})
   -\operatorname{Var}_P(Y(a))|
 \leq3P\{D(a)>g_{T,\Delta}\}=o(1)                                      \tag{1}
\]
and the quota orders imply constants \(0<c_0<C_0<\infty\) such that
\[
 c_0T^{-(1-\alpha)}\leq s_{T,\Delta}^2
 \leq C_0T^{-(1-\alpha)}.                                                \tag{2}
\]
For the lower bound, arm one suffices when \(\alpha>0\); when \(\alpha=0\), both quotas are comparable to \(T\).  The upper bound uses \(\sigma_{a,T}^2\leq1\).  The uniform studentized theorem gives
\[
 \frac{\widehat\tau_{T,\Delta}-\tau}{\widehat s_{T,\Delta}}
 =\frac{\widehat\tau_{T,\Delta}-\tau+b_{T,\Delta}}
        {\widehat s_{T,\Delta}}
  -\frac{b_{T,\Delta}}{\widehat s_{T,\Delta}},                          \tag{3}
\]
where the first term converges uniformly to \(N(0,1)\), and \(\widehat s_{T,\Delta}/s_{T,\Delta}\to1\).  The bias bound and (2) imply
\[
 \sup_{\mathfrak M_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm{reg}}(\kappa)}
 \frac{|b_{T,\Delta}|}{s_{T,\Delta}}
 \leq C_1T^{(1-\alpha)/2}(1+T+\Delta_T)^{-\beta}.                       \tag{4}
\]
If the right side tends to zero, the second term in (3) is uniformly \(o_P(1)\).  Hence the ordinary interval with critical value \(z_{1-\eta/2}\) is uniformly asymptotically honest.

For necessity, set
\[
 \delta_T=\min\{1/4,L(1+H_T)^{-\beta}\},                                \tag{5}
\]
use \(\pi_t(1)=ct^{-\alpha}\), and index a triangular family by \(\gamma\in\{-1,1\}\).  Put \(s_1=\gamma\), \(s_0=-\gamma\).  Independently over arrivals and arms, with probability \(\delta_T\) set
\[
 (D_t(a),Y_t(a))=(H_T+1,s_a),                                            \tag{6}
\]
and with probability \(1-\delta_T\) set \(D_t(a)=0\) and draw \(Y_t(a)\in\{-1,1\}\) with mean
\[
 -\frac{\delta_Ts_a}{1-\delta_T}.                                      \tag{7}
\]
The mean in (7) is admissible because \(\delta_T\leq1/4\).  For every integer \(u\geq0\),
\[
 P\{D_t(a)>u\}=
 \begin{cases}
  \delta_T,&0\leq u\leq H_T,\\
  0,&u\geq H_T+1,
 \end{cases}
 \leq\min\{1,L(1+u)^{-\beta}\}.                                      \tag{8}
\]
All outcomes are bounded and all delays are finite.  Direct calculation gives
\[
 \mathbb E_PY_t(a)=0,
 \qquad \operatorname{Var}_P\{Y_t(a)\}=1,                              \tag{9}
\]
so the construction belongs to every support-feasible regular class.  Because \(g_{T,\Delta}<h_{T,\Delta}<H_T+1\), its correction variables vanish and
\[
 b_{T,\Delta}=2\gamma\delta_T.                                          \tag{10}
\]
The visible variables have variance \(1-\delta_T-\delta_T^2\to1\).  Integral comparison gives
\[
 \frac{T^{1-\alpha}}{K_1(n_T)}\longrightarrow\frac{1-\alpha}{c},
 \qquad
 \frac{T}{K_0(n_T)}\longrightarrow\frac1\varepsilon\quad(\alpha=0).  \tag{11}
\]
Consequently, for some fixed \(s_*>0\),
\[
 T^{(1-\alpha)/2}s_{T,\Delta}\longrightarrow s_*.                       \tag{12}
\]
Since the second term in (5) is eventually active, (10)--(12) imply
\[
 \frac{b_{T,\Delta}}{s_{T,\Delta}}
 =\frac{2\gamma L}{s_*}
 T^{(1-\alpha)/2}(1+H_T)^{-\beta}\{1+o(1)\}.                            \tag{13}
\]
If the product in (13) converges to a finite positive constant, choose \(\gamma=1\).  Equation (3) then converges to \(N(-u,1)\) for some \(u>0\), and ordinary-Wald coverage converges to
\[
 \Phi(z_{1-\eta/2}-u)+\Phi(z_{1-\eta/2}+u)-1<1-\eta.                  \tag{14}
\]
The strict inequality follows by differentiating the left side with respect to \(u>0\).  If the product diverges, the centered term in (3) remains tight while the absolute shift diverges, so coverage tends to zero.  Because \(\delta_T\to0\), truncation by \([-2,2]\) is asymptotically irrelevant.  If the product fails to tend to zero, take a subsequence bounded away from zero and then a further subsequence on which it either converges to a positive finite limit or diverges.  Thus uniform honesty is impossible unless
\[
 T^{(1-\alpha)/2}(1+T+\Delta_T)^{-\beta}\longrightarrow0.              \tag{15}
\]
This proves the equivalence.  At \(\Delta_T=0\), the left side of (15) is \(T^{(1-\alpha)/2-\beta}\{1+o(1)\}\), which tends to zero exactly when \(\beta>(1-\alpha)/2=q\).

Assume \(D_t(a)=0\) almost surely for both arms.  Since \(g_{T,\Delta}\geq0\) and \(h_{T,\Delta}\geq0\) for all sufficiently large \(T\), the definitions give
\[
 X_{a,j}^{\Delta}=Y_{a,j},\qquad
 R_{a,j}^{\Delta}=0,
 \qquad U_{a,\Delta}=0.                                                   \tag{1}
\]
Also \(\mathbf 1\{D(a)>h_{T,\Delta}\}=0\), so \(b_{T,\Delta}=0\).  On quota success,
\[
 \widehat\tau_{T,\Delta}=M_{1,\Delta}-M_{0,\Delta},                    \tag{2}
\]
a difference of independent deterministic-prefix tape means.

On the regular class, the variance floor and quota orders make the largest normalized summand in (2) tend to zero.  The bounded triangular-array characteristic-function calculation in \texttt{thm:uniform-gated-inference} therefore gives a standard-normal limit, and its sample-variance calculation gives \(\widehat s_{T,\Delta}/s_{T,\Delta}\to1\).  Since quota failure has probability at most \(4T^{-4}\) and invokes the full parameter interval, \(I_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm W}\) is pointwise asymptotically honest for every such prompt-delay law.

The deterministic radius
\[
 B_{T,\Delta}=2\min\{1,L(1+h_{T,\Delta})^{-\beta}\}                    \tag{3}
\]
is a worst-case radius for the whole tail-envelope class.  It need not vanish identically under the prompt-delay specialization because \(L>0\).  Continuity and strict monotonicity of the defining equation for \(c_\eta\) give
\[
 c_\eta(u)\longrightarrow c_\eta(0)=z_{1-\eta/2}
 \qquad\text{as }u\downarrow0.                                         \tag{4}
\]
On a regular prompt-delay sequence, the quota orders, \(g_{T,\Delta}\geq T^\rho\{1+o(1)\}\), and the strict conditions on \(\rho\) also give
\[
 d_{T,\Delta}/\widehat s_{T,\Delta}\longrightarrow0.                  \tag{5}
\]
Therefore, if \(B_{T,\Delta}/\widehat s_{T,\Delta}\to0\), (4)--(5) show that the Gaussian-branch radius divided by \(\widehat s_{T,\Delta}\) converges to \(z_{1-\eta/2}\), so this branch reduces asymptotically to ordinary Wald.  Conversely, sample-variance consistency makes \(B_{T,\Delta}/\widehat s_{T,\Delta}\) asymptotically equivalent to the deterministic ratio \(B_{T,\Delta}/s_{T,\Delta}\).  If it does not tend to zero, a subsequence is bounded away from zero; strict increase of \(c_\eta(u)\) for \(u>0\) then keeps the Gaussian critical value away from \(z_{1-\eta/2}\) on a further subsequence.  Hence the stated ratio condition is also necessary for asymptotic reduction of the generic Gaussian branch to ordinary Wald.

Put \(q=(1-\alpha)/2\).  The two-sided class is contained in the one-sided class.  Indeed, \(\pi_t(1)\geq ct^{-\alpha}\), while
\[
 \pi_t(0)=1-\pi_t(1)\geq1-Ct^{-\alpha}\geq1-C\geq\varepsilon.          \tag{1}
\]
In particular, the fixed policy
\[
 p_t:=\pi_t(1)=ct^{-\alpha},
 \qquad \pi_t(0)=1-p_t                                                    \tag{2}
\]
belongs to \(\mathfrak M_T^{\mathrm{low}}\), because \(1-p_t\geq1-c\geq\varepsilon\).

For the upper bound, uniform coverage is supplied by \texttt{thm:uniform-gated-inference}.  Let
\[
 S_T=K_1(n_T)^{-1}+K_0(n_T)^{-1}.
\]
The quota lemma gives uniformly over the one-sided class
\[
 K_1(n_T)\asymp T^{1-\alpha},\quad K_0(n_T)\asymp T,
 \quad J_1\asymp T^{\rho(1-\alpha)},\quad J_0\asymp T^\rho.             \tag{3}
\]
Consequently,
\[
 S_T=O(T^{-(1-\alpha)}),
 \qquad a_T=\sqrt{2S_Tx_\eta}=O(T^{-q}).                                 \tag{4}
\]
Since \(g_{T,\Delta}\geq m_T\asymp T^\rho\),
\[
 v_{T,\Delta}=O(T^{-\rho\beta}).                                        \tag{5}
\]
For every fixed \(x>0\), (3)--(5) give
\[
 A_{1,T,\Delta}(x)
 =O\!\left(T^{-\rho(\beta+1-\alpha)/2}
          +T^{-\rho(1-\alpha)}\right)=o(T^{-q}),                        \tag{6}
\]
\[
 A_{0,T,\Delta}(x)
 =O\!\left(T^{-\rho(\beta+1)/2}+T^{-\rho}\right)=o(T^{-q}).           \tag{7}
\]
The first relations use \(\rho(\beta+1-\alpha)>1-\alpha\) and \(\rho>1/2\); the arm-zero exponents are no smaller.  The strict inequalities absorb logarithms, so
\[
 d_{T,\Delta}=o(T^{-q}).                                                  \tag{8}
\]
For observations in \([-1,1]\), the usual sample variance is at most two.  Hence, on \(E_T\),
\[
 \widehat s_{T,\Delta}^2\leq2S_T,
 \qquad \widehat s_{T,\Delta}=O(T^{-q}).                                \tag{9}
\]
Let \(z=z_{1-\eta/2}\).  Evaluating the defining coverage function at \(u+z\) gives
\[
 \Phi(z)+\Phi(2u+z)-1\geq2\Phi(z)-1=1-\eta,
\]
so monotonicity in the critical value yields
\[
 c_\eta(u)\leq u+z,
 \qquad
 \widehat s_{T,\Delta}c_\eta(B_{T,\Delta}/\widehat s_{T,\Delta})
 \leq B_{T,\Delta}+z\widehat s_{T,\Delta}.                             \tag{10}
\]
Also, uniformly over deterministic \(\Delta_T\geq0\),
\[
 \frac{1+h_{T,\Delta}}{1+H_T}
 =1-\frac{k_T}{1+H_T}=1+o(1),
 \qquad B_{T,\Delta}=O((1+H_T)^{-\beta}).                               \tag{11}
\]
Equations (4), (6)--(11) bound the length of either active branch on \(E_T\) by a constant multiple of
\[
 r_{T,\Delta}=\max\{T^{-q},(1+H_T)^{-\beta}\}.                          \tag{12}
\]
On \(E_T^c\), the interval has length four, while
\[
 4P(E_T^c)\leq16T^{-4}=o(T^{-q})=o(r_{T,\Delta}).                        \tag{13}
\]
Taking expectations proves the uniform upper bound.

For the sampling converse, retain policy (2), set both delays to zero, and set \(Y_t(0)=0\).  Let \(P_+\) and \(P_-\) give arm-one Rademacher means \(d_T\) and \(-d_T\), respectively, where
\[
 d_T=\lambda Q_T^{-1/2},
 \qquad Q_T=\sum_{t=1}^Tp_t,
 \qquad 0<\lambda<\frac{1-2\eta}{2\sqrt2}.                              \tag{14}
\]
Since \(\alpha<1\),
\[
 Q_T\asymp T^{1-\alpha},\qquad d_T\asymp T^{-q},                        \tag{15}
\]
and \(d_T<1\) eventually.  Their causal contrasts are \(\tau_+=d_T\) and \(\tau_-=-d_T\).  The one-observation Hellinger affinity of the two arm-one Rademacher laws is \(\sqrt{1-d_T^2}\).  The assignments have the same deterministic law under both alternatives, so the exact observed-experiment affinity is
\[
 \operatorname{Aff}(P_+^O,P_-^O)
 =\prod_{t=1}^T[1-p_t\{1-\sqrt{1-d_T^2}\}]
 \geq1-\sum_{t=1}^Tp_td_T^2=1-\lambda^2.                                \tag{16}
\]
Here \(1-\sqrt{1-x}\leq x\) and \(\prod_t(1-x_t)\geq1-\sum_tx_t\).  For dominated laws with affinity \(A\), Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \|P-Q\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \leq\sqrt{1-A^2}.                                                       \tag{17}
\]
Thus
\[
 \|P_+^O-P_-^O\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\leq\sqrt2\lambda.                     \tag{18}
\]
If \(J_{T,\Delta}\) is uniformly honest, transfer of the event \(\{\tau_-\in J_{T,\Delta}\}\) from \(P_-^O\) to \(P_+^O\), followed by a union bound, gives
\[
 P_+^O\{\tau_+,\tau_-\in J_{T,\Delta}\}
 \geq1-2\eta-o(1)-\sqrt2\lambda.                                      \tag{19}
\]
The right side is eventually positive.  On this event the interval length is at least \(2d_T\), so
\[
 \sup_{(P,\Pi,T)\in\mathfrak M_T^{\mathrm{low}}}
 \mathbb E_{P,\Pi}|J_{T,\Delta}|\geq c_{\eta,1}T^{-q}.                 \tag{20}
\]

For the hidden-tail converse, retain (2) and set
\[
 \delta_T=\min\{1/4,L(1+H_T)^{-\beta}\}.                               \tag{21}
\]
For each arrival and arm, independently draw a Bernoulli indicator with success probability \(\delta_T\).  On failure set \((Y_t(a),D_t(a))=(0,0)\).  On success set \(D_t(a)=H_T+1\); under \(P_+\), set the successful outcomes to \(+1\) in arm one and \(-1\) in arm zero, and under \(P_-\) reverse the signs.  Then
\[
 P_\pm\{D_t(a)>u\}=
 \begin{cases}
  \delta_T,&0\leq u\leq H_T,\\
  0,&u\geq H_T+1,
 \end{cases}
 \leq\min\{1,L(1+u)^{-\beta}\}.                                      \tag{22}
\]
Thus both alternatives are members of the one-sided class and all delays are finite.  No successful atom is revealed by \(H_T\).  The immediate zero records, absence indicators, assignments, and propensities, and therefore all of \(O_{T,\Delta}\), have identical laws under the two alternatives.  Their eventual causal contrasts nevertheless satisfy
\[
 \tau_+=2\delta_T,
 \qquad \tau_-=-2\delta_T.                                              \tag{23}
\]
Under the common observed law, honesty and a union bound yield
\[
 P\{\tau_+,\tau_-\in J_{T,\Delta}\}\geq1-2\eta-o(1).                \tag{24}
\]
On this event \(|J_{T,\Delta}|\geq4\delta_T\).  Since the second term in (21) is eventually active,
\[
 \sup_{(P,\Pi,T)\in\mathfrak M_T^{\mathrm{low}}}
 \mathbb E_{P,\Pi}|J_{T,\Delta}|
 \geq c_{\eta,2}(1+H_T)^{-\beta}.                                      \tag{25}
\]
The affinity computation (16) and the equality of observed laws preceding (23) are finite-sample identities; neither conditions on quota success or recruitment stopping.  At the Gaussian boundary, \(\alpha<1\) ensures that the rare-arm quota diverges and the maximum normalized tape summand vanishes, as derived in the gated-inference theorem.

Combining (20) and (25),
\[
 \sup_{\mathfrak M_T^{\mathrm{low}}}\mathbb E|J_{T,\Delta}|
 \geq \min\{c_{\eta,1},c_{\eta,2}\}
 \max\{T^{-q},(1+H_T)^{-\beta}\}.                                     \tag{26}
\]
Together with the upper bound, (26) proves the exact class-minimax order.  When \(\Delta_T=0\), \(H_T=T\), and (12) becomes \(\max\{T^{-(1-\alpha)/2},T^{-\beta}\}\).

For a binary endpoint, \(Y_t(a)\in\{0,1\}\subset[-1,1]\).  The stationary iid sampling and predictable randomization conditions in the statement, together with
\[
 \pi_t(1)\geq ct^{-\alpha},\qquad \pi_t(0)\geq\varepsilon,
 \qquad P\{D_t(a)>u\}\leq\min\{1,L(1+u)^{-\beta}\},                   \tag{1}
\]
place the experiment directly in \(\mathfrak M_T^{\mathrm{low}}(\alpha,\beta,L,c,\varepsilon)\).  No upper bound on \(\pi_t(1)\) is used.  Moreover,
\[
 P Y_t(1)-P Y_t(0)
 =P\{Y_t(1)=1\}-P\{Y_t(0)=1\}=\tau,                                   \tag{2}
\]
so the risk difference is the causal contrast of the potential outcomes.

Measurability follows from the construction proved in \texttt{thm:uniform-gated-inference}: assignments determine tape order and \(E_T\); a recorded revelation time determines membership in the main or correction truncation set; an absent response is known to contribute zero once its guaranteed age exceeds the truncation threshold; and the quota-failure output is \([-2,2]\).  Thus the estimator and every interval branch are functions of \(O_{T,\Delta}\), without conditioning on \(E_T\) or requiring propensity convergence.

For an explicit concentration guarantee, let \(\widetilde\tau_{T,\Delta}\) be the unconditional virtual fixed-prefix estimator.  The bounded independent tape variables and the exponential chord inequality give, with \(S_T=K_1(n_T)^{-1}+K_0(n_T)^{-1}\),
\[
 P\left\{\left|(M_{1,\Delta}-\mathbb E_PM_{1,\Delta})
 -(M_{0,\Delta}-\mathbb E_PM_{0,\Delta})\right|>
 \sqrt{2S_Tx}\right\}\leq2e^{-x}.                                     \tag{3}
\]
For each old-tail mean, boundedness and the delay envelope give
\[
 P\left\{|U_{a,\Delta}-\mathbb E_PU_{a,\Delta}|>
 \sqrt{\frac{2v_{T,\Delta}x}{J_a}}+\frac{4x}{3J_a}\right\}
 \leq2e^{-x}.                                                            \tag{4}
\]
The old-cohort identity states
\[
 \mathbb E_P\widetilde\tau_{T,\Delta}=\tau-b_{T,\Delta},
 \qquad |b_{T,\Delta}|\leq B_{T,\Delta}.                               \tag{5}
\]
Taking \(x=x_\eta=\log(6/\eta)\) in (3)--(4), a union bound gives
\[
 P\{\tau\notin I_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm{conc}}\text{ on }E_T\}
 \leq6e^{-x_\eta}=\eta.                                                 \tag{6}
\]
On \(E_T^c\), the full interval \([-2,2]\) contains \(\tau\).  Hence the concentration interval is honest unconditionally.  The gated-inference theorem proves the corresponding uniform honesty of the hybrid and, on the regular subclass, its studentized Gaussian assertion.

We next prove the necessity of the ordinary-Wald condition within binary outcomes.  Put
\[
 x_T=T^q(1+H_T)^{-\beta},
 \qquad
 \delta_T=\min\left\{\frac14,\frac L2(1+H_T)^{-\beta}\right\},        \tag{7}
\]
and use the deterministic policy \(\pi_t(1)=ct^{-\alpha}\).  For \(\sigma\in\{-1,1\}\), set \((r_1^\sigma,r_0^\sigma)=(1,0)\) if \(\sigma=1\), and \((0,1)\) if \(\sigma=-1\).  Independently over arrivals, define
\[
 (D(a),Y(a))=
 \begin{cases}
  (H_T+1,r_a^\sigma),&\text{with probability }\delta_T,\\
  (0,Z_a^\sigma),&\text{with probability }1-\delta_T,
 \end{cases}                                                            \tag{8}
\]
where
\[
 Z_a^\sigma\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}\!\left(
 \frac{1/2-\delta_Tr_a^\sigma}{1-\delta_T}\right).                    \tag{9}
\]
The probability in (9) lies in \([0,1]\).  For \(0\leq u\leq H_T\),
\[
 P\{D(a)>u\}=\delta_T
 \leq\frac L2(1+H_T)^{-\beta}\leq L(1+u)^{-\beta},                    \tag{10}
\]
and the tail is zero for \(u\geq H_T+1\).  Thus the law satisfies the delay envelope.  Direct calculation gives
\[
 \mathbb E_PY(a)=\frac12,
 \qquad \operatorname{Var}_P\{Y(a)\}=\frac14,                          \tag{11}
\]
so \(\tau=0\).  Because the delayed component lies beyond \(h_{T,\Delta}\), it enters neither correction, and
\[
 b_{T,\Delta}=\delta_T(r_1^\sigma-r_0^\sigma)=\sigma\delta_T.           \tag{12}
\]
The quota formula gives
\[
 K_1(n_T)\sim\frac{c}{1-\alpha}T^{1-\alpha},
 \qquad K_0(n_T)\sim\varepsilon T.                                     \tag{13}
\]
The visible Bernoulli probabilities tend to \(1/2\), so for some \(\gamma\in(0,\infty)\),
\[
 T^q s_{T,\Delta}\longrightarrow\gamma,
 \qquad
 \gamma^2=
 \begin{cases}
  (1-\alpha)/(4c),&\alpha>0,\\
  (c^{-1}+\varepsilon^{-1})/4,&\alpha=0.
 \end{cases}                                                            \tag{14}
\]
The second term in the minimum in (7) is eventually active, whence
\[
 \frac{|b_{T,\Delta}|}{s_{T,\Delta}}
 =\frac{L}{2\gamma}x_T\{1+o(1)\}.                                      \tag{15}
\]
The family is regular with floor \(1/4\) if \(\alpha>0\) and floor \(1/2\) if \(\alpha=0\).  The uniform studentized theorem therefore gives, along any subsequence on which the right side of (15) tends to \(u\in(0,\infty)\),
\[
 \frac{\widehat\tau_{T,\Delta}-\tau}{\widehat s_{T,\Delta}}
 \Rightarrow N(-\sigma u,1).                                           \tag{16}
\]
For \(z=z_{1-\eta/2}\), the limiting coverage is
\[
 \Phi(z-u)+\Phi(z+u)-1<1-\eta.                                         \tag{17}
\]
If (15) diverges, the absolute shift diverges while the centered term remains tight, so coverage tends to zero.  Every failure of \(x_T\to0\) has a subsequence of one of these two kinds.  Hence uniform honesty of unpadded ordinary Wald over the one-sided class requires
\[
 T^q(1+T+\Delta_T)^{-\beta}\longrightarrow0.                            \tag{18}
\]
Conversely, \texttt{prop:wald-followup-frontier} proves that (18) is sufficient on \(\mathfrak M_{T,\Delta}^{\mathrm{reg}}(\kappa)\).  Without that variance floor, (6) and the gated-inference theorem supply the stated uniformly honest alternatives.

It remains to solve (18).  If \(\Delta_T=0\) and \(\beta>q\), then
\[
 T^q(1+T)^{-\beta}=T^{q-\beta}\{1+o(1)\}\longrightarrow0.             \tag{19}
\]
If \(\beta=q\),
\[
 T^q(1+T+\Delta_T)^{-q}\longrightarrow0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \frac{\Delta_T}{T}\longrightarrow\infty.                             \tag{20}
\]
If \(\beta<q\), positivity and taking the \(\beta\)-th root give
\[
 T^q(1+T+\Delta_T)^{-\beta}\longrightarrow0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \frac{T+\Delta_T}{T^{q/\beta}}\longrightarrow\infty.                 \tag{21}
\]
Finally, prompt-delay laws have \(b_{T,\Delta}=0\), so the tail obstruction is class-wide rather than pointwise.  The sampling converse in the minimax theorem uses prompt delays and is compatible with outcome--delay independence; only the hidden-tail witness (8) deliberately uses informative delay.
